name: Religious communism
summary: Religious communism holds that common ownership of goods is commanded or modelled by religion, most often by the Jerusalem church of Acts, whose members shared everything and gave to each as he had need. Its adherents live or seek to live in voluntary communities of goods, work the land together and reject buying, selling and hired labour as a betrayal of faith. Within this family, the Hutterites and Winstanley's Diggers renounce force, while Müntzer's peasant movement took up arms.
scope: The mainstream Christian strand: the Jerusalem church of Acts, the Hutterite colonies, and Winstanley's Diggers, with Müntzer, the Taborites and Oneida noted as variants. Islamic, Buddhist and Taiping cases, and Marxist-religious blends, are excluded. Because these groups wrote little on modern policy, many answers are low-confidence inferences.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Winstanley condemned buying and selling of land and Christian communists cite love of money as the root of evil, so market allocation is rejected on principle.

unions-good.rationale: Religious communists were rarely concerned with trade unions; communal work replaces the wage relation unions bargain over.

property-fundamental.rationale: Acts 4:32 says no one claimed any possession as their own, directly denying private property as a fundamental right.

cut-welfare.rationale: Sharing so that none lacks need is the core ethic of the early church, so cutting aid for fear of dependency is opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Working the land together and holding the product in common resembles collective ownership by those who labour, though the unit is the community.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Hutterite and similar communities impose strict moral rules, while Diggers said nothing; adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Winstanley held that no person should rule over another, and Hutterite colonies elect and can remove their leaders.

state-harmful.rationale: Winstanley and Hutterites distrust rulers and worldly separation, but few strands call for abolishing all government; they run their own disciplined communities.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nonresistance bars Hutterites from military roles and Winstanley abhorred force, so more military and police power is disfavoured.

decide-locally.rationale: Decision-making sits in the colony or congregation, with its own council and vote, favouring small local self-rule.

traditional-family.rationale: Hutterites keep patriarchal family units, but Taborites, Oneida and Diggers varied; strands are split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is the source and centre of the movement, and communities organise life around scripture, though they seek separation from the state.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Loyalty is to the religious community, not the nation; Hutterites preserve their own language and customs instead.

gradual-change.rationale: Movements aimed at an immediate reorganisation of life on communal lines rather than slow reform of existing institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Buying and selling for gain is condemned by Winstanley and by Christian communists citing 1 Timothy 6:10.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nonresistance and rejection of force make military intervention difficult to endorse even for rights.

revolution-justified.rationale: Winstanley and Hutterites renounce armed force, though Müntzer in the Peasants' War is a violent counter-example, so the mainstream is against.

experts-over-public.rationale: Winstanley held that each person has the same inner reason as any ruler, against deference to elites.

central-planning.rationale: Communities coordinate production inside the colony by consent, not by a state plan; a central state plan is not their model.

socialized-markets.rationale: Winstanley rejects markets altogether, while Hutterite colonies trade with outsiders; split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy between states is outside what Acts, the Diggers or Hutterites wrote about; neutral.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They favour common ownership, not many small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Winstanley rejected giving or taking hire, and Hutterites work without paychecks, though money is still used for outside trade.

one-party-rule.rationale: Communities are governed by their congregation and elected ministers under scripture, not a party; Winstanley rejected rule of one over another.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Taborites rejected their king and Winstanley denied any right of one to rule another.

democracy-best.rationale: Hutterite colonies vote internally but not on liberal terms; adherents place divine law above majorities.

direct-votes.rationale: Colonies decide major matters by membership vote, but the sources do not extend this to national lawmaking.

natural-rulers.rationale: Winstanley stated all are equals in creation and none was ordained to rule another.

political-violence-never.rationale: Winstanley abhorred arms and Hutterites hold nonresistance, though Müntzer's strand was violent.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of force reject war as ennobling.

separate-church-state.rationale: Hutterites and Anabaptist-descended groups hold worldly separation and keep the state out of the church, though they want exemptions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Hutterite Ordnungen and scripture-based rules govern life in colonies; they seek a society ordered by scripture, not state law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hutterites avoided secular courts, yet no stand on private provision of defence.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Religious communism is contrasted with Marxism, and class conflict is not its explanatory frame; Engels read Müntzer that way instead.

civilizational-union.rationale: Fellowship is of believers within a community; not political union of nations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement rests on renouncing private gain, with the love of money condemned as evil.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Members owe the community obedience under the Ordnungen and share goods as a duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Winstanley saw earth as a common treasury given for all, valued by use; not clearly addressed.

direct-action.rationale: Diggers occupied commons and began working the land themselves rather than petitioning Parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: Winstanley said community would be built by working together, without force.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Diggers and Hutterites are agrarian, not foragers.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Colonies assign roles by gender and office, and not abolish them.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Acts 2:45 and 4:35 say distribution was made to each as he had need, the founding text of the strand.

production-for-use.rationale: Common treasury and working together for all to eat describes production for use not profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Winstanley treated hired labour as upholding the curse and profit from trade as unrighteous.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Religious communism is contrasted with Marxism, and its voluntary and religious strands do not seek class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Diggers worked land together and Hutterite colonies farm collectively as the main economic form.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a doctrine of the strand; Marxist claims are not its own.

taxation-theft.rationale: Hutterites refuse to pay taxes for war but accept ordinary taxes; not a principle.

harm-principle.rationale: Colony rules regulate whole lives and conduct beyond harm to others.

conscription.rationale: Nonresistance bars Hutterites from military service and led them to emigrate from Russia over conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Members may leave but are shunned; voice is limited; mixed.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts the rejection of buying and selling for gain.

positive-liberty.rationale: Meeting need so that none lacks is the ethic, but freedom language is not used.

organic-representation.rationale: Colonies are governed by councils and elected bosses, but this isn't family-and-trade-body representation.

total-state.rationale: Communities seek separation from the state and refuse state control.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority is not by oaths to lords, and Winstanley rejects lording.

bound-labor.rationale: Winstanley denied any person's right to labour owed to another, calling for equals.

single-common-good.rationale: One heart and soul and a common treasury aim at one common good.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Colonies hold member votes and elect their managers, who can be removed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Freedom of the market is rejected; liberty is found in community of goods.

rule-by-example.rationale: Early church and colonies rely on exemplary conduct and discipline rather than state law; Winstanley used inner reason.

national-self-determination.rationale: The community of believers, not the nation, is the unit of self-rule, so the sources give no answer on national states.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religious communism springs from principles native to religion; Winstanley grounded his case in inner anointing.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class conflict is not its frame; but wage employment is rejected.

workers-nation.rationale: Believers are one humankind; neither national nor class lines.

ban-interest.rationale: The biblical condemnation of usury is cited by Christian communists as a basis against interest.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist doctrine rather than a religious communist one; but Winstanley saw rulers as oppressors.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claims are not part of the strand.

national-mission.rationale: Worldly separation and nonresistance counter mission by state.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Winstanley supports equality while Hutterites are patriarchal; split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Winstanley and the Diggers saw rulers and landlords as oppressors of the poor.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Equal moral worth of all persons.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mutual care for need is a duty, not left to a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Winstanley called all equals in creation and Christian communism stresses one humankind.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Communities seek their own law and exemptions, but no stance on civil code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Anabaptist-descended groups stress voluntary membership and religious liberty for themselves.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a socialist state in the Soviet sense, and rejection of state power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Colony leaders are elected and removable by member vote; Winstanley rejected rule imposed by one on another.

trade-surplus.rationale: Commerce for gain is not an aim.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorring arms mean initiating force is wrong, though property rights are not the reason.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fellowship and sharing replace struggle for gain.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Communities seek exemptions from the state, so empowering it to ban parties is not favoured.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Winstanley said none should lord over another, matching non-domination.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party is Marxist-Leninist, whereas religious communism acts by congregation and conscience.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distribution to need so that none lacks, with the poor central in the early church.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Winstanley blamed buying and selling and landlords for want, not numbers.

party-commands-army.rationale: The strand rejects armies and party rule.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Church discipline binds members but parties are not the model.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan, not part of the strand; nonresistance but no stated stance.

recall-officials.rationale: Hutterite ministers and bosses are elected and can be removed by vote.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Nonresistance and separation from worldly powers.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Diggers and Hutterites chose agrarian communal life as the model.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hutterites limit schooling at around age 15, yet no stated stance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The sources do not take up ranking of cultures; neutral, though Christian universalism cuts both ways.

minority-language-support.rationale: Hutterites maintain their German church language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Hutterites repeatedly sought exemptions on photo ID and military service.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social conformity is enforced through Ordnungen and shunning.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sharing with those in need is the ethic of the movement.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of arms make a national nuclear arsenal incompatible with the Hutterite and Digger stance.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In Acts property is sold and brought to the community so that none lacks.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances conflict with nonresistance, so an attack on one ally being an attack on all is rejected.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hutterites resist state control and secular courts, with the state curbing church property disfavoured.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nonresistance means military force cannot be used to hold a region, whatever the political merits.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Winstanley held no one is to lord over another.

character-from-environment.rationale: The sources attribute change to conversion and shared life rather than giving a theory of character; neutral.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule by one over others rejected.

leader-cult.rationale: Honouring a human ruler runs against equality and God as sole authority.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist topic not at issue.

land-redistribution.rationale: Winstanley wanted land held in common and taken from those who monopolise it, though by peaceful occupation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Hutterites shun those who leave but stress voluntary membership; the state punishing is not backed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Hutterite women wear head coverings by custom, not law; split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Colonies seek their own culture and institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Contrasted with Marxist materialism; they hold religious principles drive change.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work is done from fellowship and love rather than pay, as in colonies where members receive only allowances.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Taborites rejected feudal lords and Winstanley rejected one lording over another.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not found in the sources on religious communism; neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: Colony leaders are elected, and rulers by inheritance are not favoured.

minority-veto.rationale: Hutterite decisions by vote of members, but unanimity is not required; split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Taborites and Müntzer resisted, whereas Winstanley and Hutterites renounce force.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Winstanley's equality placed no one above, and Hutterites put scripture over legislation.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Hutterites hold worldly separation and avoid political involvement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Hutterites ban television for moral reasons, but not framed this way.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is Marxist and absent from the sources on religious communism; neutral.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns Marxist parties' national paths, which is not the strand's concern; neutral.

paid-care-work.rationale: Colonies treat care work as communal service without pay; split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Colony officers can be removed by vote of the members.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Sharing in common provides for the old, not individual savings.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Giving up possessions and the love of money condemned.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of arms rule out funding armed groups abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of arms rule out troops entering allied countries without consent.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Hutterite colonies teach obedience under the Ordnungen, though they refuse state demands that violate conscience.

non-intervention.rationale: Separation from the world and nonresistance.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Church marriage is central to colony life.

local-production.rationale: Colonies produce for themselves from local land.

informal-organisation.rationale: Diggers formed small voluntary groups working land together.

religious-nation.rationale: They separate the believing community from the nation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Oneida members kept few personal items and Hutterites have personal allowances, though all else is common.

defeat-communism.rationale: Adherents are communists in their own sense, and see religion as the source.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religious communism is contrasted with Marxism, which called for eliminating religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Capitalism is condemned as founded on love of money.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Winstanley and Taborites emphasise equality yet the strand rarely links it to economics; split.

socialized-care.rationale: Hutterite colonies share communal meals and care; strands differ.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing communal settlements are the central form: Jerusalem church, Diggers, Hutterite colonies.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: They call themselves communists, though not in the Marxist sense.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Conservative strands would disapprove, but state punishment is rejected by others; split.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Nonresistance; the Islamic strand differs, but the mainstream is Christian.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Colonies decide by member votes; Winstanley's equals.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The sources do not frame their politics by left and right; neutral.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx compared work in common to a remedy, and the strand condemns hired labour.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Winstanley and Hutterites ground authority in God, not human rulers.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Hutterites seek religious exemptions and practices.

dynastic-succession.rationale: No ruling of one over another.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Usury condemned and common aid favoured.

property-franchise.rationale: Winstanley's insistence that all are equals in creation excludes limiting the vote to owners, and the strand rejects private property in land.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept of commodity relations that the sources do not use, though the strand opposes buying and selling; neutral.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equality of all in creation (Winstanley) and one humankind rules out a racial franchise.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Winstanley said land kept in the hands of a few is theft.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Religion is central to the strand, opposed to Marxist elimination.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about community or state ownership of land, and the statement now asks only whether a right to hold land should end when the holder stops using it.

reviewHistory.rationale: Winstanley made the earth a common treasury and Hutterite colonies own land as a body, so individuals hold it only as members.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Acts and the Hutterite colonies meet need through voluntary sharing inside the believing community, with no state role.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Hutterite family roles are patriarchal, and the other strands wrote little against it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Winstanley and the Hutterites reject living off hire and property and share the fruits of common labour, though Acts distributes by need.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Hutterites hold nonresistance even against attack, and the Diggers acted without violence; Muntzer is the exception.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Hutterites honour martyrs of the faith but not those who die for a nation, as they refuse force.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Muntzer, Winstanley and the Hutterites all see worldly power as opposed to God's order and set communal life against it.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Hutterites and Diggers sought renewal through exemplary communities, not by capturing a state.

municipal-property.rationale: Goods are held in common by the local community, whether the Jerusalem church, a Hutterite colony or a Digger commune.

person-over-state.rationale: Believers give up private goods for the community, yet reject coercive rulers; the strands do not give one answer.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement is founded on religion, treating common ownership as a commandment of faith.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement's shared-goods ethic is universal among believers and Winstanley held all equal in creation.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Hutterites and Diggers renounce force, and the sources contrast Müntzer's armed variant as exceptional.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Hutterites and Diggers renounce force and bear no arms, so they favour minimal armaments, though Müntzer's wing took up arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Hutterites hold nonresistance and refuse military service, and the Diggers renounced force, though Müntzer's strand fought.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Müntzer's strand sought to overthrow rulers, but Hutterites withdraw from the state and the Diggers acted nonviolently; the family is split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Winstanley grounds equality in all people's common creation by God, and Acts treats believers as sharing one standing before God.

workers-own-party.rationale: Communities of goods stand outside party politics (Hutterites abstain, Diggers sought no party), while the Müntzer strand was a mass movement; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Hutterites abstain from politics while Muntzer sought a godly rule by force; no common view on defining democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Hutterite colonies enforce strict traditional moral discipline, and Acts treats sexual morality as a matter for the community.

women-suffrage.rationale: Hutterite colonies are patriarchal and men vote on colony affairs, so equal political rights are not part of their practice.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Winstanley called the earth a common treasury not to be bought or sold, and Acts has believers holding all things common.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Acts-based and Hutterite communities treat the Bible as authoritative and live by it directly, though Winstanley's reading was spiritual and allegorical.

simple-living.rationale: Shared goods and limited personal needs are the core of life in Acts and in Hutterite colonies.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Winstanley's Standard holds the earth a common treasury for all, made so by creation, and that those who fence it in wrong the rest.

police-more-powers.rationale: Nonresistance bars Hutterites from military roles and Winstanley abhorred force, so more military and police power is disfavoured. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Sharing so that none lacks need is the core ethic of the early church, so cutting aid for fear of dependency is opposed. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Believers should live in a community where members hold their goods in common.
missingStatements.rationale: Acts 2:44 and 4:32 describe believers holding all things common, and Hutterites still live this way.

missingStatements.text: No person should work for hire for another or rent land from another.
missingStatements.rationale: Winstanley pledged to work together without giving or taking hire.

missingStatements.text: The Earth belongs to all people in common and should not be bought and sold.
missingStatements.rationale: Winstanley called the earth a common treasury and condemned its sale to a few.

notes: Strands differ on violence (Hutterites and Diggers nonresistant, Müntzer armed) and on gender (Hutterites patriarchal, Taborites and Winstanley egalitarian). Many modern policy answers are inferred from the Hutterites' conservative practice. Sources on Wikipedia, Hutterite and Christian communism pages were read in part only (first 100,000 characters).
